mainTopic: Who pays whom when a stolen item is sold and the thief is identified, and where תקנת השוק applies
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's case of an owner who finds his stolen things with someone else. רב אשי explains that a rumor of theft in the city settles that they were stolen, not sold. Next comes a מחלוקת between רב and רבי יוחנן about a thief who sold an item and was later identified: does the owner claim from the thief or from the buyer? רב יוסף says they do not really disagree, and אביי pushes back. The גמרא then gives three explanations of what they argue about, ending with רב פפא's view that the argument is about תקנת השוק, the Sages' rule protecting buyers. The גמרא then maps out where תקנת השוק applies: pledges, sales and overpriced sales are covered, but paying off an old debt or credit tab is not. Two stories apply these rules: אבימי's stolen cloak, where the הלכה follows רב כהן, and a stolen scroll sold twice, where רבא makes the owner refund the last buyer in full. Finally a new משנה begins about a man who pours out his own wine to save another man's honey.

steps.title: No need for further investigation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that in this case one does not need to look into the matter in so much detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not need to look into it this much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling from the previous discussion and says the court does not have to investigate any further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous discussion describes an owner who is known not to sell his belongings. Because of this, the court can rely on that fact and does not need to dig deeper into how the items left his house.

keyTerms.meaning: To pursue, to look around and check into something

phrases.english: One does not need to pursue it
phrases.notes: This line ends a ruling that began just before this section, about someone known not to sell his belongings.

phrases.english: all this much.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צָרִיךְ לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי עֲלֵיהּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owner is known not to sell his belongings, no further investigation is needed.

steps.title: Maybe he needed money and sold it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling: even someone who usually does not sell his things might have needed cash and sold these items.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he needed money and sold them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ruling. Even a person who normally keeps his things might have sold them once because he needed money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depended on the idea that this person does not sell his belongings. The challenge points out that this habit is not proof, because anyone can be pressed for cash. If he did sell the items, the buyer is the rightful owner.

phrases.english: But perhaps he needed money, and he sold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reliance on the owner's habit of not selling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the owner's habit of not selling is enough to trust him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A habit is not proof. Someone who needed money could have sold the items this one time.

steps.title: The rumor of theft settles it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a rumor of theft spread in the city, so we do not suspect that he sold the items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: A rumor of theft spread in the city.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. The case is one where the whole city heard that this man's things were stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two facts together make his claim believable: he does not usually sell his belongings, and there is public talk that he was robbed. With the rumor, the idea that he sold the items for money is no longer a real worry.

keyTerms.meaning: A reputation or rumor of theft
Look, there has gone out about him

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי יָצָא לוֹ שֵׁם גְּנֵיבָה בָּעִיר.
phrases.english: There went out a rumor of theft about him in the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הֲרֵי יָצָא לוֹ שֵׁם גְּנֵיבָה בָּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact to the case: there is a public rumor of theft.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner might have sold the items because he needed money.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since there is a rumor of theft, we accept that the items were stolen, not sold.
steps.whatToRemember: The owner is believed because of two facts together: he does not usually sell his belongings, and a rumor of theft spread in the city.

steps.title: Thief identified after selling: claim against the thief
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a thief stole and sold, then was identified. רב, in the name of רבי חייא, says the owner's claim is with the first one, the thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If a thief stole and sold, and later the thief was identified, רב said in the name of רבי חייא: The claim is with the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. When the thief is now known, רב says the owner can only go after the thief, not the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the thief was unknown. Now the thief is known, so the question is whether the owner takes the item back from the buyer or collects from the thief. רב's view is that the owner deals only with the thief.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim is with the first one (the thief)

phrases.english: It was stated: If one stole and sold,
and afterward the thief was identified –
Rav said in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya:
The claim is with the first one.
phrases.notes: "The first one" is the thief, the first person to hold the item after the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: גָּנַב וּמָכַר, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּכַּר הַגַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the unknown-thief case to a case where the thief is identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב in the name of רבי חייא: the owner claims only from the thief.

steps.title: Opposing view: claim against the buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ינאי, says the claim is with the second one, the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ינאי: The claim is with the second one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing opinion. רבי יוחנן says the owner can go after the buyer, the second person to hold the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to clash directly with רב. רב says the owner deals with the thief, while רבי יוחנן says he can take his item back from the buyer. The next step will ask whether they really disagree.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
The claim is with the second one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the opposite position to רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי ינאי: the owner can claim from the buyer.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Before or after giving up hope
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says they do not disagree. Before יאוש the claim is with the buyer, and after יאוש the claim is with the thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They do not disagree. Here it is before יאוש, so the claim is with the second one. There it is after יאוש, so the claim is with the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the clash between רב and רבי יוחנן by showing they are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer bought before the owner gave up hope, the item still belongs to the owner and he takes it from the buyer, like רבי יוחנן. If the buyer bought after יאוש, the owner's hold on the item is gone (יאוש together with the change of hands), so he can only claim from the thief, like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner's giving up hope of getting the item back

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order. רבי יוחנן, who said "the second," is matched with before יאוש. רב, who said "the first," is matched with after יאוש. רב יוסף mentions the "second" case first.
steps.whatToRemember: Before יאוש the owner takes his item from the buyer. After יאוש he can only go after the thief.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how important יאוש is for deciding when a stolen item stops belonging to its original owner.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: They do not disagree;
here, it is before despair –
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's case: the buyer bought it before the owner gave up hope.

phrases.english: the claim is with the second one,
there, it is after despair –
the claim is with the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each opinion refers to a different situation (before or after יאוש).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רבי יוחנן seem to disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree. Before יאוש the claim is against the buyer, and after יאוש it is against the thief.

steps.title: Both אמוראים accept רב חסדא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that both רב and רבי יוחנן agree with רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both of them hold like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his answer that רב and רבי יוחנן do not disagree. He adds that both of them follow the ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא ruled that before יאוש, the owner may claim from either the thief or the buyer. So both אמוראים agree on the case before יאוש, and they only seem to argue because each is talking about a different stage.

phrases.english: And both of them hold
the ruling of Rav Ḥisda.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא said that before יאוש, the owner can go after either the thief or the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's reconciliation from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sides accept a shared earlier ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: רב and רבי יוחנן do not disagree; both follow רב חסדא.

steps.title: אביי: they do disagree in the case of priestly gifts
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. In the case of מתנות כהונה, which are like 'before יאוש', רב and רבי יוחנן do argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And they don't disagree? But priestly gifts are like a case before יאוש, and they do disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's claim that the two אמוראים agree. He points to a case that counts as 'before יאוש' where they still argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they agree before יאוש, they should agree about מתנות כהונה, since a כהן never gives up on his gifts. אביי says there is an argument there, so רב יוסף's split between before and after יאוש cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts from an animal that are given to a כהן
Are treated like a case before the owner gave up

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And they don't disagree?
But gifts of the priesthood
are like a case before despair,
phrases.notes: The כהנים never give up on these gifts, so they are like a stolen item before the owner gave up.

phrases.english: and they do disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reconciliation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רב and רבי יוחנן agree before יאוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a case like 'before יאוש', priestly gifts, where they do argue, so the split by stage does not hold.

steps.title: The משנה about buying a cow's innards
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה. If someone buys a cow's innards and the priestly gifts are inside, he must give them to a כהן. Whether he may subtract their value from the price depends on whether he bought by weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if someone told a butcher 'Sell me a cow's innards' and the priestly gifts were in them, he gives them to a כהן and does not subtract their value from the price. If he bought by weight, he gives it to a כהן and does subtract it from the price.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the source for his challenge, a משנה about a butcher selling innards that contain the כהן's gift. This sets up the next step, where רב comments on this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the buyer must hand the gift to a כהן. The difference is only about money. When he bought a general amount, he does not subtract. When he paid by weight, he paid for the gift too, so he may subtract its value.

phrases.english: As we learned: he said to him:
"Sell me the innards of a cow,"
and the gifts were in them –
he gives them to a priest,
and he does not deduct it from the price.
If he bought from him by weight –
he gives it to a priest,
and he deducts it from the price.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, אָמַר לוֹ: מְכוֹר לִי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind אביי's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That רב and רבי יוחנן argue in a case like 'before יאוש'
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in חולין about buying innards containing מתנות כהונה

steps.title: רב: if the butcher weighed it, the claim is with the butcher
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the משנה to a buyer who weighed for himself. If the butcher weighed, the כהן's claim is with the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: They only taught this where the buyer weighed it for himself. But if the butcher weighed it for him, the claim is with the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes אביי's proof. רב says that when the butcher did the weighing, the כהן goes after the butcher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The butcher who sold the כהן's gift is like a thief, and the buyer is like the purchaser. אביי reads רב as saying the claim is ONLY with the butcher, even though this is like 'before יאוש'. That is how אביי shows a real argument exists even before יאוש.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of…

phrases.english: And Rav said: They taught this only
where he weighed for himself,
but if the butcher weighed for him –
the claim is with the butcher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁשָּׁקַל לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by quoting רב's ruling on the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב holds the claim is only against the 'thief' (butcher) even in a case like before יאוש

steps.title: רב means the כהן can ALSO claim from the butcher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's reading. רב means the כהן may also claim from the butcher, and he needed to teach this so we would not think priestly gifts cannot be stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that רב meant: the claim is also with the butcher. You might have thought that priestly gifts cannot be stolen, so רב teaches us that they can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. רב's words do not mean 'only the butcher'; they mean 'the butcher too'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב means 'also', then the כהן can claim from either the buyer or the butcher. That matches רב חסדא's rule for before יאוש, so there is no argument. רב still needed to say it, because otherwise we might think a butcher never 'steals' the gifts, since they always stay the כהנים' property.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's reconciliation stands: before יאוש the owner, or here the כהן, can claim from either side. רב only added that the butcher is also a valid target.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הַדִּין עִם הַטַּבָּח' as 'only with the butcher'. The whole answer depends on reading it as 'also with the butcher'.

phrases.english: Say: the claim is also with the butcher.
You might have said:
gifts of the priesthood cannot be stolen,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's reading of רב's statement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof that רב and רבי יוחנן argue before יאוש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי read רב as 'only with the butcher'; it can mean 'also with the butcher'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Priestly gifts can be stolen, and the כהן may claim from the butcher as well as from the buyer, so there is no proof of an argument.

steps.title: What exactly do they disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to אביי, who said that רב and רבי יוחנן disagree, what is the point of their disagreement?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, who said they disagree, what do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just pushed back on אביי's proof. It now asks: according to אביי, who holds that רב and רבי יוחנן argue, what is the argument actually about? This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had said that both agree with רב חסדא. אביי's proof that they argue was pushed aside, but he still holds that they argue. If so, we need to know the exact issue between them.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, who said they disagree,
phrases.notes: "They" means רב and רבי יוחנן, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's position that רב and רבי יוחנן argue, and asks for the content of their argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact halachic point on which רב and רבי יוחנן disagree, according to אביי.

steps.title: They disagree about רב חסדא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they disagree about the ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the argument is about רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not accept רב חסדא's ruling, so the owner may collect only from the thief. רבי יוחנן accepts it, so the owner may collect from either the thief or the buyer.

phrases.english: About the ruling of Rav Ḥisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether רב חסדא's ruling is correct. רב rejects it and רבי יוחנן accepts it.

steps.title: רב זביד: the owner gave up only after the buyer had the item
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד gives a different answer. The argument is about a case where the owner gave up hope only after the item reached the buyer, not while the thief had it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: for example, when the owners gave up hope while the item was with the buyer, but had not given up hope while it was with the thief.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד offers a second explanation of the dispute and names the exact case they argue about. The next step explains why they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, both agree that before any יאוש the owner can claim from either the thief or the buyer. They argue only when the יאוש came late, after the item had already moved to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave up hope of getting the item back (יאוש)

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
For example, where the owners gave up hope while it was in the buyer's hands,
but did not give up hope while it was in the thief's hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּתְיָיאֲשׁוּ הַבְּעָלִים בְּיַד לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 12, instead of the רב חסדא explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about a case where the יאוש happened only after the item reached the buyer.

steps.title: Does the order of יאוש and change of owner matter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the buyer owns the item only if יאוש came before the change of possession. רב holds that the order makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they argue about. One Sage holds: יאוש and then change of possession, the buyer acquires; change of possession and then יאוש, he does not acquire. The other Sage holds: there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב זביד's case. The two sides disagree about whether the order of events matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the buyer acquires only if the owner gave up hope before the item moved to him. Here the item moved first, so the owner can still claim it from the buyer. For רב, any יאוש together with a change of possession lets the buyer acquire, so the owner cannot take it from the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting the item back
Change of possession: the item moves to a new person

steps.confusionAlert: The order is what matters here. In this case the item moved to the buyer first and the יאוש came after. That is exactly the case where רבי יוחנן says the buyer does not acquire.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב זביד, רבי יוחנן holds that יאוש must come before the change of possession for the buyer to acquire. רב holds that the order does not matter.

phrases.english: And this is what they disagree about:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: יֵאוּשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ שִׁינּוּי רְשׁוּת – קָנֵי,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: despair and afterward a change of possession, he acquires;
phrases.notes: The first "מר" is רבי יוחנן, and the second "מר" below is רב.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁינּוּי רְשׁוּת וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵאוּשׁ – לָא קָנֵי;
phrases.english: a change of possession and afterward despair, he does not acquire;
and the other Sage holds: there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle behind the case רב זביד named in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the buyer acquires only if יאוש came before the change of possession. רב: the order makes no difference.

steps.title: רב פפא: the cloak goes back, and they argue about תקנת השוק
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees the stolen cloak goes back to its owner. The argument is only about whether תקנת השוק was applied in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: about the cloak itself, everyone agrees that it goes back to its owner. Here they argue about whether the Sages applied תקנת השוק to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third explanation of the dispute. The sentence ends with a dash, which tells us the גמרא is about to explain this disagreement in more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא moves the argument away from who owns the cloak, since all agree it returns to its owner. The only question is whether the market rule, תקנת השוק, applies here. That rule concerns the buyer who paid for the item.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak (the stolen item in the case)
The Sages' rule protecting buyers in the marketplace

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: regarding the cloak itself,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּהָדַר לְמָרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it goes back to its owner;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּעָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק קָמִיפַּלְגִי –
phrases.english: and here they disagree about whether they applied the marketplace provision to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question of step 12, instead of the explanations of steps 13 and 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone agrees the cloak goes back to its owner. They argue only about whether תקנת השוק applies here.

steps.title: Who the buyer collects from: the thief or the owner
steps.stepSummary: רב, in the name of רבי חייא, says the buyer collects only from the thief and there is no תקנת השוק. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ינאי, says the buyer collects from the owner because תקנת השוק applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said in the name of רבי חייא: the buyer's claim is with the first one, the thief. The buyer takes his money back from the thief, and the Sages did not apply תקנת השוק here. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ינאי: the buyer's claim is with the second one. The buyer takes his money from the owner, and the Sages did apply תקנת השוק here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two opinions behind רב פפא's answer. Both agree the cloak goes back to the owner. They only argue about who pays the buyer back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תקנת השוק is a rule the Sages made so that honest buyers are not scared away from the market. רב says it does not apply here, so the buyer must chase the thief for his money. רבי יוחנן says it does apply, so the owner pays the buyer what he spent and then takes his item back.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages' rule protecting the market: an innocent buyer gets back what he paid when he returns a stolen item to its owner
The claim is against the first one, the thief

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya:
The claim is with the first one,
phrases.notes: "The first one" means the thief, as the next words explain.

phrases.english: meaning that the law for the buyer
is that he takes his money from the thief,
and they did not apply the market rule in this case.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
The claim is with the second one,
meaning that the law for the buyer is that he takes his money from the owner,
and they did apply the market rule in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר הַדִּין עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two positions inside רב פפא's answer, which said the argument is only about תקנת השוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the buyer collects from the thief, with no תקנת השוק. רבי יוחנן: the buyer collects from the owner, with תקנת השוק.

steps.title: Challenge from רב הונא's ruling on חנן בישא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רב really hold there is no תקנת השוק? His student רב הונא told an owner to pay the buyer back in the case of the thief חנן בישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold that the Sages did not apply תקנת השוק here? But רב הונא was רב's student. When חנן בישא stole a cloak and sold it, and the case came before רב הונא, he told the owner: Go redeem your pledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's opinion. It points to a ruling by רב's own student that seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חנן בישא's case the thief was identified, so it matches the case being discussed. רב הונא made the owner pay the buyer to get his cloak back, which is exactly תקנת השוק. Since a student normally follows his teacher, this suggests רב did hold of תקנת השוק here.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked חנן, a man known for his wickedness
Go redeem your pledge, meaning pay the buyer and take back your item

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַב לֹא עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק?
phrases.english: And does Rav hold that they did not apply the market rule here?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲוָה,
phrases.english: But Rav Huna was Rav's student,
and Chanan the Wicked stole a cloak and sold it.
The case came before Rav Huna,
and he said to that man, the owner:
Go redeem your pledge!
phrases.notes: He means: pay the buyer back and take your cloak, as if you were getting back something you had left as a pledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב לֹא עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק? וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's position as stated in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that there is no תקנת השוק when the thief is known
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's student applied תקנת השוק in a case where the thief was identified, so רב must hold the same.

steps.title: חנן בישא had no money, so he counts as unknown
steps.stepSummary: The case of חנן בישא is different. The buyer could not collect from him, so it is treated like a case where the thief was never identified.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן בישא is different. Since there is no way to collect payment from him, it is as if the thief was not identified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that רב הונא's ruling does not go against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds there is no תקנת השוק only when the buyer can really collect from the thief. חנן בישא could not pay, so the buyer had no real way to get his money. This is like a case where the thief is unknown, and there everyone agrees תקנת השוק applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a case where the thief was not identified

phrases.english: Chanan the Wicked is different,
since there is no way to get paid from him,
it is like a case where the thief was not identified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב הונא's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's ruling shows that רב holds of תקנת השוק even when the thief is known.
steps.terutzMaskana: A thief who cannot pay is treated like an unknown thief, so תקנת השוק applies to him even according to רב.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a known thief who has no money is treated like an unknown thief, so the buyer collects from the owner.

steps.title: רבא: no market protection for a well-known thief
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that if the seller is a well-known thief, the Sages did not apply תקנת השוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he is a well-known thief, the Sages did not apply תקנת השוק here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule. A buyer who buys from a famous thief does not get the market protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תקנת השוק protects honest buyers who had no reason to suspect anything. Someone who buys from a well-known thief should have known better. So the Sages gave him no protection, and the owner does not have to pay him.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he is a well-known thief,
they did not apply the market rule to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם גַּנָּב מְפוּרְסָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new limit on תקנת השוק, separate from the רב and רבי יוחנן argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer from a well-known thief does not get תקנת השוק.

steps.title: But חנן בישא was well known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: חנן בישא was well known, yet רב הונא applied תקנת השוק to his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חנן בישא was well known, and still they applied תקנת השוק in his case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule using the story of חנן בישא from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His nickname shows that everyone knew he was a bad man. If a well-known thief gets no תקנת השוק, רב הונא should not have made the owner pay the buyer. Yet he did.

keyTerms.meaning: But here is a case where...

phrases.english: But Chanan the Wicked was well known,
and they applied the market rule to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a well-known thief gets no תקנת השוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנן בישא was famous, yet רב הונא applied תקנת השוק in his case.

steps.title: Known as a villain, not as a thief
steps.stepSummary: חנן בישא was famous for being a bad person, but not for stealing, so רבא's rule did not apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he was known for being wicked, but he was not known for stealing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps רבא's rule in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule only covers someone famous as a thief. חנן בישא was known as a bad man in other ways, so a buyer had no reason to think his cloak was stolen. That is why the buyer still got תקנת השוק.

phrases.english: Granted that he was well known for wickedness,
he was not well known for stealing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any well-known bad person counts as a 'well-known thief.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone known specifically for stealing loses the buyer his תקנת השוק.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule removes תקנת השוק only when the seller is known as a thief. Being known as a bad person in general is not enough.

steps.title: Paying off a debt with a stolen item gets no market protection
steps.stepSummary: If a thief uses a stolen item to pay off an old debt or a store tab, the creditor gets no תקנת השוק. He never gave anything with this item in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if a thief stole something and used it to pay off his debt, or to pay off his store tab, the חכמים did not apply תקנת השוק. We tell the creditor: you did not give him anything because of these items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching about when תקנת השוק does not apply. The case is a thief who uses stolen goods to pay off money he already owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תקנת השוק protects someone who handed over money for the item. Here the creditor gave the loan or the credit long before, without this item in mind. So he gets no protection, and the owner simply takes his item back.

keyTerms.meaning: The market enactment: the owner repays the innocent holder what he paid before taking back his item
His store credit, a tab he ran up by buying on credit
With the intention of, with this in mind

phrases.english: It was stated: if he stole and paid off his debt with it,
or he stole and paid off his store credit with it –
they did not apply the market enactment in this case,
because they say: it was not with these in mind
that you gave him anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the חנן בישא discussion, the גמרא opens a new set of rulings that map out where תקנת השוק applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor who received stolen goods as payment of an existing debt or store credit gets no תקנת השוק, because he gave nothing with those goods in mind.

steps.title: A pledge worth double the loan does get market protection
steps.stepSummary: If a thief gave a stolen item worth 200 as a pledge for a loan of 100, the lender gets תקנת השוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pledge: if the item was worth two hundred and was given for a loan of one hundred, they applied תקנת השוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case, a stolen item given as a pledge for a loan. When the item is worth much more than the loan, the lender is protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from step 23. Here the lender handed over his money because of this item, which is what the reason in step 23 was missing. So the owner must repay the lender the loan amount before taking back his item.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge, an item given to a lender as security for a loan

phrases.english: A pledge: worth two hundred, given for a hundred –
phrases.notes: The stolen item is worth 200 and was handed over as security for a loan of 100.

phrases.english: they applied the market enactment in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from paying an old debt to a new loan secured by a stolen pledge, where תקנת השוק does apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender who took a stolen item worth 200 as a pledge for a loan of 100 receives תקנת השוק.

steps.title: A pledge equal to the loan: אמימר and מר זוטרא disagree
steps.stepSummary: If the pledge is worth exactly the loan amount, אמימר says there is no תקנת השוק and מר זוטרא says there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the pledge and the loan are of equal value, אמימר said: they did not apply תקנת השוק. מר זוטרא said: they did apply תקנת השוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with the pledge case. It now asks what happens when the item is worth only as much as the loan, and two אמוראים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees about a pledge worth double the loan, as we saw in step 24. The question is whether that protection still holds when the item and the loan are equal. אמימר says no and מר זוטרא says yes. The text does not give their reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal for equal: the item is worth exactly the loan amount

phrases.english: If it was equal for equal – אמימר said:
phrases.notes: Still talking about the pledge, but now the item is worth just the amount of the loan.

phrases.english: they did not apply the market enactment in this case,

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק.
phrases.english: מר זוטרא said: they did apply the market enactment in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the pledge case from step 24 to an equal-value pledge, where there is a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a pledge equal in value to the loan, אמימר denies תקנת השוק and מר זוטרא grants it.

steps.title: The הלכה follows מר זוטרא: an equal-value pledge is protected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that תקנת השוק does apply to a pledge equal in value to the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: they did apply תקנת השוק in this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute from step 25. The practical ruling follows מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in practice, the lender is protected whether the pledge is worth more than the loan or exactly the same. In both cases the owner must repay the loan amount to get his item back.
steps.whatToRemember: A stolen pledge is covered by תקנת השוק whether it is worth more than the loan or the same amount.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: they did apply the market enactment in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the אמימר and מר זוטרא dispute in favor of מר זוטרא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that תקנת השוק applies even to a stolen pledge equal in value to the loan.

steps.title: A sale at a fair price gets market protection
steps.stepSummary: If someone bought a stolen item for what it is really worth, he gets תקנת השוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sale: if he paid equal value for it, they applied תקנת השוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from pledges to sales. It starts with the simple case, a buyer who paid a fair price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the classic case תקנת השוק was made for. An innocent buyer paid fair market price, so the owner must pay him back before taking the item. This sets up the harder case in the next step.

phrases.english: A sale: equal for equal –
they applied the market enactment in this case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the pledge cases to the case of a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer who paid fair value for a stolen item receives תקנת השוק.

steps.title: A buyer who paid double: רב ששת and רבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: If an item worth 100 was bought for 200, רב ששת says there is no תקנת השוק and רבא says there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the item was worth one hundred and he bought it for two hundred, רב ששת said: they did not apply תקנת השוק. רבא said: they did apply תקנת השוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the harder sale case, where the buyer paid far more than the item is worth. Two אמוראים disagree about whether he is protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a fair price, everyone agrees there is protection (step 27). Here the buyer overpaid, paying double the item's value. רב ששת holds this buyer gets no תקנת השוק, while רבא holds he does. The text does not give their reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth one hundred, bought for two hundred

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the pledge case in step 24. There the item was worth 200 and secured only 100. Here it is the opposite: the item is worth 100 and the buyer paid 200.

phrases.english: If it was worth a hundred, bought for two hundred –

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: לֹא עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: רב ששת said: they did not apply the market enactment in this case,

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק.
phrases.english: רבא said: they did apply the market enactment in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁוֵי מְאָה בְּמָאתַן – רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fair-price sale of step 27 with an overpriced sale, where there is a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a stolen item worth 100 bought for 200, רב ששת denies תקנת השוק and רבא grants it.

steps.title: Final rule: תקנת השוק applies except for paying old debts
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that תקנת השוק applies in all the earlier cases, except where a thief paid off a debt or a credit tab with the stolen item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is that in all these cases the Sages made תקנת השוק, except when a thief stole and paid his debt, or stole and paid off his credit tab.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling for all the cases it just discussed (pledges, purchases, overpaying, and so on).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case where someone gave real money or a loan in exchange for the stolen item, he gets back what he paid. But if the item only paid off an old debt, the receiver did not lay out anything new because of it. So there is no market reason to protect him.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final ruling)
The Sages' market ordinance: an innocent buyer gets his money back from the owner

steps.whatToRemember: תקנת השוק protects someone who paid out money because of the item. It does not protect someone who only had an old debt paid off with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This exception is the rule that the coming story turns on.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: in all of them
they made the market ordinance,
except for one who stole and paid his debt,
or stole and paid off his credit tab.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: בְּכוּלְּהוּ עָשׂוּ בּוֹ תַּקָּנַת הַשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on all the preceding cases, including the מחלוקת in step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תקנת השוק applies everywhere except paying a debt or a credit tab with a stolen item.

steps.title: The story of אבימי and the stolen cloak
steps.stepSummary: A man who owed אבימי four זוזים gave him a stolen cloak. אבימי then lent him four more. The thief was found out, and the case came to רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי בר נאזי, רבינא's father-in-law, was owed four זוזים by a certain man. The man stole a cloak and brought it to him, and אבימי lent him four more זוזים. In the end the thief was identified, and the case came before רבינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case. It is setting up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two loans here. The first was made before the cloak arrived, and the second was made after it. The question will be how the rule from the last step applies to each loan.

phrases.english: Avimi bar Nazi, father-in-law of Ravina,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: was owed four zuz by a certain man.
He stole a cloak and brought it to him,
and he lent him four more zuz.
In the end the thief was identified.
It came before Ravina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבִימִי בַּר נָאזִי חֲמוּהּ דְּרָבִינָא הֲוָה מַסֵּיק בְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a practical case that tests the exception just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case. No ruling is given yet.

steps.title: רבינא splits the two loans
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that the first four זוזים get nothing, because that was paying off a debt. For the second four, אבימי takes his money from the owner and returns the cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The first ones count as 'stole and paid his debt,' so the owner does not need to give him anything. For those other four זוזים, take your money and return his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies the rule from step 29 to each loan separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first loan was an old debt, so the exception applies and there is no תקנת השוק. רבינא treats the second loan as given because אבימי was holding the cloak. That makes it like a loan on a pledge, so תקנת השוק does apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ones (the first four זוזים)

phrases.english: He said: the first ones —
he stole and paid his debt,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתַּב לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי;
phrases.english: so he does not need to give him anything at all;
those other four zuz —
take your money, and return his cloak.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, so read it as 'and return his cloak.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבינא's ruling on the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First loan: no תקנת השוק. Second loan: תקנת השוק applies, as if the cloak were its pledge.

steps.title: רב כהן: maybe the second loan was just trust
steps.stepSummary: רב כהן argues that the cloak may have been payment only for the first loan, and the second loan was given on plain trust, just like the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהן objects: But maybe he gave him the cloak for those first זוזים, which is 'stole and paid his debt, stole and paid his credit tab.' And the last four זוזים were lent because he simply trusted him, just as he trusted him at the start!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהן challenges רבינא's ruling on the second loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed the second loan was made because of the cloak. רב כהן says there is no proof of that. The cloak was handed over as payment, and אבימי may have lent again on trust alone. If so, the second loan has nothing to do with the cloak, and תקנת השוק does not apply to it either.
steps.confusionAlert: רב כהן does not dispute the first loan. He only questions whether the cloak had any connection to the second loan.

phrases.english: Rav Kohen objects to it:
But perhaps the cloak — for those first zuz
he gave it to him,
'stole and paid his debt, stole and paid his credit tab';
phrases.notes: He is quoting the exception from step 29.

phrases.english: and the last four zuz —
he simply trusted him,
just as he trusted him at the start!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב כֹּהֵן: וְדִלְמָא גְּלִימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבינא's ruling on the second loan.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's ruling that the second four זוזים get תקנת השוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing shows the cloak was security for the second loan. It may have been given purely on trust, so the cloak is tied only to the old debt.

steps.title: רבי אבהו rules like רב כהן
steps.stepSummary: The case reached רבי אבהו, who ruled according to רב כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter went around until it reached רבי אבהו, who said: the הלכה follows רב כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows רב כהן, so אבימי gets no תקנת השוק for either loan. He must return the cloak, and the owner owes him nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter rolled on (went from court to court)

steps.whatToRemember: If a stolen item was given as payment for an old debt, later loans are not assumed to be tied to it. There is no תקנת השוק unless the money was clearly given because of the item.

phrases.english: The matter rolled on,
and it reached Rabbi Abbahu,
who said: the halacha follows Rav Kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיגַּלְגַּל מִילְּתָא, מְטָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רבינא and רב כהן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב כהן: neither loan gets תקנת השוק.

steps.title: A stolen scroll is sold twice
steps.stepSummary: A thief from נרשא stole a ספר and sold it to a man from פפוניא for 80 זוזים. That man resold it to a man from מחוזא for 120 זוזים. Then the thief was caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man from נרשא stole a scroll and sold it to a man from פפוניא for eighty זוזים. The man from פפוניא then sold it to a man from מחוזא for 120 זוזים. In the end the thief was identified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. It is setting up a court case so the next steps can rule on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time there are two sales. The first buyer bought straight from the thief, and the second buyer bought from an honest buyer at a higher price. The question will be how much each person has to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A man from the town of נרשא (here, the thief)
A man from the town of פפוניא (the first buyer)
A man from the town of מחוזא (the second buyer)

phrases.english: A man from Naresh stole a scroll,
and sold it to a man from Pappunya for eighty zuz.
The man from Pappunya went

phrases.aramaic: זַבְּנֵיהּ לְבַר מָחוֹזָאָה בִּמְאָה וְעֶשְׂרִין זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: and sold it to a man from Mechoza for one hundred and twenty zuz.
In the end, the thief was identified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical case that applies the תקנת השוק rule from step 29, now with two buyers in a row.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case facts: stolen ספר sold for 80, resold for 120, thief later identified.

steps.title: אביי: the owner pays 80, and the last buyer collects 40 from his seller
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the owner gives the man from מחוזא 80 זוזים and takes back his ספר. The man from מחוזא then collects the remaining 40 from the man from פפוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The owner of the scroll should go and give the man from מחוזא eighty זוזים and take his scroll. Then the man from מחוזא should go and take forty from the man from פפוניא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his ruling on the case. The owner only refunds the original price of 80.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי counts the תקנת השוק refund only at the price the thief got, 80. The extra 40 that the second buyer paid came from the middle buyer's profit, so the second buyer has to collect it from him.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Let the owner of the scroll go

phrases.aramaic: וְיָהֵב לֵיהּ לְבַר מָחוֹזָא תְּמָנַן זוּזֵי
phrases.english: and give the man from Mechoza eighty zuz
and take his scroll back,
and then the man from Mechoza goes
and takes forty from the man from Pappunya.
phrases.notes: That 40 is the profit the man from פפוניא made when he resold the scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case described in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner refunds only 80 (the thief's sale price). The last buyer recovers the extra 40 from the middle buyer.

steps.title: רבא: a buyer from a buyer deserves protection even more
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if the תקנת השוק protects someone who bought straight from a thief, it surely protects someone who bought from an honest buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Now, if the חכמים made the תקנת השוק for someone who buys from a thief, is there any question about someone who buys from a buyer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's ruling with a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man from מחוזא never dealt with the thief at all. He bought from a regular buyer, so he deserves the market protection even more. That means he should get back everything he actually paid, 120, from the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys from a buyer

phrases.english: Rava objects to this:
Now, if for one who buys from a thief
they made the market enactment for him,
then one who buys from a buyer, is it even a question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's ruling in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that the owner refunds only 80.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: someone who bought from an honest buyer is more deserving of the תקנת השוק than someone who bought from a thief, so he should get his full price back from the owner.

steps.title: רבא: the owner pays 120, then collects 40 from the middle buyer and 80 from the thief
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the owner pays the man from מחוזא the full 120 to get his ספר back. Then he collects 40 from the man from פפוניא and 80 from the thief.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The owner of the scroll should give the man from מחוזא 120 זוזים and take his scroll. Then the owner should collect forty from the man from פפוניא and eighty from the man from נרשא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's ruling with his own. The last buyer gets his full price, and the owner then recovers his money from the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person pays back what he gained. The middle buyer made 40 in profit, so he returns 40. The thief received 80, so he returns 80. In the end the owner is made whole at 120.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ruling replaces אביי's: the last buyer gets back his full price from the owner. The owner then collects from each earlier person exactly what that person gained.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who collects the 40. In אביי's version the man from מחוזא collects it. In רבא's version the owner collects it, because he already paid the full 120.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Let the owner of the scroll go

phrases.aramaic: וְיָהֵיב לֵיהּ לְבַר מָחוֹזָאָה מְאָה וְעֶשְׂרִין זוּזֵי
phrases.english: and give the man from Mechoza one hundred and twenty zuz
and take his scroll back,
and then let the owner of the scroll go
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and collect forty from the man from Pappunya,
and eighty from the man from Naresh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא gives his own ruling, based on his challenge in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner pays the last buyer his full 120, then collects 40 from the middle buyer and 80 from the thief.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the תקנת השוק protects every buyer in a chain at the price he actually paid. Each earlier party then pays back what he gained.

steps.title: New משנה: pouring out your own wine to save someone else's honey
steps.stepSummary: Two men are traveling, one with a barrel of wine and one with a jug of honey. The honey container cracks, and the wine owner pours out his wine to save the honey in his barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One man came with his barrel of wine and another came with his jug of honey. The honey container cracked, and the first man poured out his wine and saved the honey into his barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, and this step only sets up the case. The ruling on what the honey owner must pay comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new topic is someone who gives up his own property to save another person's more valuable property. The question being set up is whether he gets paid back for his wine, or only a worker's wage.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
This one came with his barrel of wine,
and that one came with his jug of honey;
the barrel of honey cracked,
and this one poured out his wine
and saved the honey into it,
phrases.notes: "Into it" means into his own wine barrel, which he just emptied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: saving another person's property at a loss to yourself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup only: the wine owner poured out his wine to save the other man's honey. The ruling follows.
